name: Hikaru Utada
label: Epic Records Japan
lede: She cut a record at thirteen, made the best-selling album in Japanese history at sixteen, then went to America, walked away, and came back making songs about her mother and a video game.

eras.title: A record man's kid in Manhattan
eras.text: Born in New York to a producer and an enka singer, writing songs by ten, recording a first album at thirteen. The music exists years before anyone in Japan hears it.

years.h: Hikaru Utada is born in New York to two people in the music business
years.p: Father Teruzane Utada is a record producer; mother [[Keiko Fuji|3d5ebe93-dfa1-434f-807f-ddab40247c4b]] is an enka singer. Utada grows up on the Upper East Side before moving to Tokyo at eleven.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Utada started writing music and lyrics around age ten and later attended Seisen International School and the American School in Japan. The father-daughter team would co-produce every Japanese album through Fantôme.

years.h: Cubic U: a thirteen-year-old cuts an R&B album at Sony Music Studios
years.p: Sessions for the future Precious run August 5-20 in New York, with producers including Teruzane Utada, Keiko Fuji and Booker T. Jones.
years.xp: Cubic U was the stage name and the name of the R&B backing band, according to Wikipedia. The same source puts a limited single, "I'll Be Stronger", in 1996 too. Nothing here reaches a wide audience yet.

eras.title: The one record that reset Japan
eras.text: A flop under the name Cubic U, then a Japanese-language debut that becomes the country's best-selling album. Eleven months separate the two.

years.h: Precious by Cubic U: a Carpenters cover and no chart entry
years.p: The English-language debut, on Toshiba EMI, failed to chart on release and was never commercially distributed in the US.
years.xp: Lead single "Close to You" is the Burt Bacharach and Hal David song the Carpenters made famous. After First Love, Precious was reissued on March 31, 1999 and reached No. 2 on the Oricon weekly albums chart with 702,060 copies, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Automatic" and "Time Will Tell" arrive as a double single
years.p: The first Japanese-language Utada single comes out three months before First Love and sets up the album.

years.h: First Love: 2,026,870 copies in week one, from a sixteen-year-old
years.p: Recorded on weekends around school in New York, Los Angeles and Tokyo, it becomes the best-selling album in Japanese history.
years.xp:
Wikipedia cites 8.7 million copies in Japan and about 18 million worldwide, and says it is the only album certified octuple million by the RIAJ. Utada described the ingredients as a computer, an MD player, time, a desire to express and a deadline. Ted Jensen mixed at Sterling Sound in New York.

The album sits at No. 99 on Rolling Stone Japan's 2007 list of the 100 greatest Japanese rock albums. A 15th anniversary edition in 2014 was capped at 10,000 copies after starting at 5,000.

years.h: Taiwan adopts "First Love" as its No. 1 song of the year
years.p: Wikipedia reports 500,000 copies of the album in Taiwan, the best seller by a Japanese act there, and a marching-song slot at the 2000 national high school baseball tournament.

eras.title: Three straight million-sellers, and a game
eras.text: Distance and Deep River lock in the run that no other Japanese act has matched, and a video game director's phone call opens a second career.

years.h: Distance sells 3,002,720 copies in a week, same day as Ayumi Hamasaki
years.p: Hamasaki's A Best came out the same day and debuted at No. 2. Utada and Hamasaki both said the rivalry was a label creation.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the matchup a "label-sponsored campaign", with both singers frustrated by it. The album was made with American producers including Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis and Rodney Jerkins, and it runs R&B through jazz, hip-hop and rock. It went on to sell over 4.4 million in Japan per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Blow My Whistle": Foxy Brown, Pharrell and Chad Hugo, for Rush Hour 2
years.p: A US soundtrack collaboration reaches No. 11 on the Billboard 200 and tops the soundtracks chart, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Hikari" becomes the first Kingdom Hearts theme
years.p: Director Tetsuya Nomura asked for Utada personally; the English version, "Simple and Clean", plays in the international game.
years.xp:
Nomura said he was "absolutely thrilled when she agreed". "Hikari" debuted at No. 1 on Oricon with 270,370 copies and was No. 10 for the year. In 2008 Guinness World Records listed it as the best-selling video game single in Japan, per Wikipedia.

Utada re-recorded both versions in 2024 with [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]].

years.h: Deep River makes it three albums past three million
years.p: No other singer or group in Japan had three in a row, Wikipedia says; first week was 2.35 million.
years.xp: The singles were "Traveling", "Hikari" and "Sakura Drops/Letters". Wikipedia lists it as the eighth best-selling album in Japanese history, with over 3.6 million sold.

years.h: Utada marries film director Kazuaki Kiriya
years.p: Kiriya directs the "Passion" video and the film Casshern, which gets an Utada theme in 2004; they divorce in March 2007.

eras.title: Utada takes on America
eras.text: Three albums under the name Utada for Island Def Jam and Island, with Timbaland and Stargate on the desk. Japan buys them. The US mostly doesn't.

years.h: Exodus: Timbaland, Island Def Jam, and No. 160 on the Billboard 200
years.p: "Devil Inside" tops the US dance club chart; the album sells over a million in Japan and about 55,000 in the US per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Released in Japan September 8 and North America October 5, 2004. "Easy Breezy" did not chart. AllMusic heard "urbane, modern, and avant-garde electronica"; other critics split on the lyrics and the bid for a Western market.

years.h: "Passion" and "Sanctuary" carry Kingdom Hearts II
years.p: Utada said "Hikari" was the dawn and "Passion" felt like dusk. It peaked at No. 4 with 49,242 first-week copies.
years.xp: "Passion" is the fourth single from Ultra Blue (June 2006); "Sanctuary" is the English version. Recorded at Westlake in California and Bunkamura in Tokyo, per Wikipedia, with a video by Kiriya. Wikipedia reports about 350,000 sold.

years.h: "Flavor of Life" sells two million downloads before it has a physical release
years.p: The ballad version, from the drama Hana Yori Dango 2, is the first single to do that, per Wikipedia; EMI put it over 7.7 million by July.
years.xp: The drama's producers asked for something like "First Love". Three versions exist: the synth-pop original, the ballad and the CD-only "antidote mix".

years.h: "Beautiful World" starts the Evangelion run
years.p: The theme for Evangelion 1.0 is the first of four Rebuild films Utada writes for; the video never shows the singer.

years.h: This Is the One: Stargate, Tricky Stewart and Sephora listening parties
years.p: The US push peaks at No. 69 on the Billboard 200; Utada leaves Island and drops the Utada name afterward.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists about 300,000 sold worldwide and a US promotional run of radio tours, Sephora listening parties and TV spots on KTLA and The Early Show. AllMusic's David Jeffries praised the polish but called most lyrics clichéd; the Japan Times' Daniel Robson called it "bland, accessible and predictable".

eras.title: Time off, and a loss
eras.text: A stated break that lasts six years, bracketed by a farewell concert streamed to the world and the death of Utada's mother.

years.big: Two years or five, no promise
q: I don't know if it will be 2 years or 5 years.
years.h: Utada announces a break from music
years.p: A blog post says the focus since age fifteen has narrowed life, and promises new music first.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Utada cited wanting a broader range of experiences after devoting ages 15 to 27 to music. Single Collection Vol. 2 followed on November 24, 2010, with five new tracks, and landed at No. 1 with 231,000 first week.

years.h: Wild Life: two Yokohama Arena nights, streamed to Ustream's record
years.p: Wikipedia gives 345,000 unique viewers and a Ustream record for simultaneous viewers.

years.h: "Sakura Nagashi" ends the quiet, on YouTube first
years.p: Written after the March 2011 Tohoku earthquake for Evangelion 3.0 with Paul Carter; Naomi Kawase directs the video. It peaks at No. 2 on Billboard Japan.

q: I am proud to be the daughter of my mother.
years.h: [[Keiko Fuji|3d5ebe93-dfa1-434f-807f-ddab40247c4b]], Utada's mother, dies
years.p: Japan Today reported it as an apparent suicide; Utada wrote about her publicly days later.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the death to August 22, 2013. In a statement Japan Today dated August 26, Utada said the way her mother ended her life was "beyond sad" and that she remembered only her laughing. Wikipedia ties the themes of Fantôme to this loss.

eras.title: Fantôme and the Epic years
eras.text: The comeback album is a record of grief. Then a move to Sony's Epic, a Kingdom Hearts III song with Skrillex, and the A. G. Cook collaboration that sets up Bad Mode.

years.h: Fantôme: the comeback that opens with a mother's death
years.p: [[Sheena Ringo|9e414497-23b7-4ab7-9ec6-8ea9864c9e87]] duets, KOHH guests, and the album spends four weeks at No. 1 in Japan.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Sheena Ringo on "Nijikan Dake no Vacance" and KOHH on "Bōkyaku". It debuted at 252,581 copies, won Album of the Year at the Japan Record Awards and is certified three-times platinum. All three singles were digital-only.

years.h: Utada leaves EMI for Sony's Epic label
years.p: The March 2017 move ends nearly two decades on Toshiba EMI and its successors; the back catalogue hits streaming in January 2018.

years.h: Hatsukoi, first album for Epic, enters at No. 1
years.p: Debuted atop Oricon's physical and digital charts, with over 242,000 sold per Wikipedia.
years.xp: "Hatsukoi" is the title of the album and of a single released May 30, 2018. Utada had by then divorced a second spouse; Wikipedia gives April 2018.

years.cap: Picture from "Hikaru Utada Laughter in the Dark Tour 2018" · Wikimedia
years.h: "Face My Fears" with Skrillex and Poo Bear
years.p: Utada asked Skrillex for a remix of "Chikai"; he proposed a new song. It becomes Utada's first Billboard Hot 100 entry, No. 98.
years.xp: "Chikai" ("Don't Think Twice" in English) is the game's ending theme. Wikipedia calls "Face My Fears" Utada's first original English song since This Is the One and says it reached No. 9 on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs. The CD single followed January 18, 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: One Last Kiss (Hikaru Utada song)
years.h: "One Last Kiss" closes the Evangelion saga
years.p: Hideaki Anno directs the video after Utada asks him; A. G. Cook co-produces.
years.xp: It reaches No. 1 on Billboard Japan's Hot 100 and Oricon's combined chart, per Wikipedia, and No. 40 on Billboard's Global 200. Utada said the film is about loss and grief.

years.h: Utada comes out as nonbinary on an Instagram livestream
years.p: Uses she/her and they/them, per Wikipedia, and says Ms. and Mrs. never fit.

eras.title: Bad Mode, and a catalogue looked at again
eras.text: A bilingual album made across the pandemic, with PC Music and Floating Points in the room, and a twenty-fifth anniversary.

years.h: Bad Mode: Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and ranked it No. 31 of 2022
years.p: The album is co-produced with [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]], [[Floating Points|69d9c5ba-7bba-4cb7-ab32-8ccc48ad4f97]], Skrillex and Poo Bear, and sings in both Japanese and English.
years.xp:
Joshua Minsoo Kim wrote the Pitchfork review, per Wikipedia. Slant ranked it No. 9 of 2022; Gorilla vs. Bear put it at No. 19. It topped Oricon and Billboard Japan, finished No. 26 on Oricon's year-end chart and went Gold from the RIAJ with 166,698 certified units.

Recorded between 2018 and 2021; the physical release followed on February 23, 2022. The Japan Times called it "a career highlight".

years.h: Live Sessions from Air Studios hits Netflix
years.p: A studio concert film of Utada's songs, released on Netflix.

years.h: A 25th-anniversary best-of, Science Fiction, is announced
years.p: A Japan, Taiwan and Hong Kong tour follows in 2024; Utada re-recorded "Hikari" and "Simple and Clean" with A. G. Cook in 2024.

sources.title: Wikipedia: One Last Kiss (Hikaru Utada song)
